summary.business: Cemindia Projects Limited (formerly ITD Cementation India Limited) is an engineering and construction company that designs and builds civil infrastructure for government, PSU and private clients across maritime structures, metro rail, airports, highways/bridges/flyovers, industrial structures and buildings, hydro dams/tunnels/irrigation, water and wastewater, foundation and specialist engineering, and data centres. It operates across 16 Indian states with an overseas presence in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the UAE.

currentContext.strengths: Over 90-year civil engineering legacy and execution track record across maritime structures, metro rail, airports, highways, bridges/flyovers, industrial structures, data centres, hydro dams, tunnels and irrigation|Strategic integration with the Adani Group providing enhanced financial strength, improved access to capital, shared procurement capabilities, global vendor networks and early visibility into a large infrastructure project pipeline|Diversified, all-time high order book of Rs 24,545 crores across a geographically spread footprint (16 Indian states plus Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and UAE)|Technology-enabled execution framework: Building Information Modelling (BIM), IoT-enabled asset intelligence, UAV site monitoring, and an integrated Project Management Information System (PMIS)|Modern, specialised construction equipment fleet including Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs), trench cutters, jack-up barges, batching plants and hydraulic piling rigs|Large, experienced professional workforce of 3,187 permanent employees plus 33,621 contractual personnel|Well-balanced client mix across government (58%), PSU (36%) and private (6%) clients mitigating concentration risk
currentContext.strategies: Maintaining a conservative and resilient balance sheet|Accelerating digital transformation to enhance execution visibility and efficiency|Diversifying the order book across geographies and high-growth sectors|Strengthening organisational capability, operational agility and execution excellence|Continuing focus on maritime structures, urban transit systems, multimodal logistics, airports, urban infrastructure, Tier II and Tier III city development, and digital infrastructure, pursued selectively with disciplined bidding practices and capital prudence|Strategic expansion into the fast-growing data centre sector, combined with integrated civil, structural and specialised MEP capabilities, to deliver projects end-to-end|Systematically building a diversified project portfolio engineered to capture large-scale, technically demanding infrastructure opportunities|The Board recommended a dividend of Rs 3 per equity share for FY 2025-26 (on 17,17,87,584 equity shares of Re 1 each), subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, under a Dividend Distribution Policy maintained per Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Management has publicly characterised its balance sheet as conservative and prudently managed, citing credit-rating strength as evidence of financial discipline even as the Company scales operations.
currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26, Cemindia secured record order inflows of Rs 14,821 crores, taking the order book to an all-time high of Rs 24,545 crores as of March 31, 2026, spanning a diversified project mix across maritime structures, metro rail, airports, highways/bridges/flyovers, industrial structures and buildings, hydro dams/tunnels/irrigation, water and wastewater, foundation and specialist engineering, and data centres. Major new orders secured during the year include a four-laning road project in Bihar, the Pune underground metro (Maharashtra), EPC of a data centre in Maharashtra, the Kolkata underground metro (West Bengal), bulk and breakwater works for a Greenfield captive jetty in Odisha, airport works at Jaipur International Airport (Rajasthan) and Trivandrum International Airport (Kerala), LNG jetty works in Abu Dhabi, breakwater and container berth Phase II works at Vizhinjam (Kerala), and a multi-storeyed commercial building in Kolkata. The Company is expanding into the fast-growing data centre segment, including 80 MW (NMI-03) and 30 MW (NMI-01) data centres at Ghansoli, Maharashtra. Growth is supported by continued investment in a modern, specialised construction equipment fleet (Tunnel Boring Machines, trench cutters, jack-up barges, batching plants, hydraulic piling rigs) and digital execution tools (Building Information Modelling, IoT-enabled asset intelligence, UAV site monitoring, and an integrated Project Management Information System). Capital expenditure directed toward technologies that improve environmental and social impact rose to 6.33% of total capex in FY26 from 3.90% in FY25 (BRSR Principle 2), including adoption of BSVI-compliant diesel generator sets and an HVS Rotating Laser Machine (150 metre) to improve construction quality and efficiency.
currentContext.mdna: India's infrastructure sector is entering a multi-decade investment cycle supported by transformative government initiatives such as the National Infrastructure Pipeline, Sagarmala, Bharatmala and PM Gati Shakti, driving opportunities across transportation, urban infrastructure, maritime structures and data centres|FY 2025-26 performance marks a strategic transition toward high-value mega-projects, which management says is driving considerable margin expansion and superior execution quality|Structural challenges flagged by management include macroeconomic volatility, input cost fluctuations, working capital intensity and industry-wide skill shortages, mitigated through disciplined bidding, prudent financial management and sustained investment in talent and operational capabilities|Integration into the Adani Group is expected to enhance the ability to undertake larger, more complex, multidisciplinary infrastructure projects while preserving engineering discipline and execution excellence|Total value of new contracts secured during FY 2025-26 exceeded Rs 14,821 crores, including several major contracts of Rs 200 crores and above across metro tunnels (West Bengal, Pune), water intake systems (Uttar Pradesh), a four-laning road project (Bihar), port/berth and breakwater works (Odisha, Kerala), data centres (Maharashtra), and international jetty and container terminal works (Abu Dhabi, Colombo)|During the year a number of contracts were completed, including underground metro sections in Mumbai and Kolkata, a rubble mound breakwater in Kerala, a bulk berth at Dhamra (Odisha), a marine jetty in Tamil Nadu, container terminal works in Colombo (Sri Lanka), and the Brahmaputra riverfront development in Assam|The Company is systematically diversifying its project portfolio across geographies and high-growth sectors to capture large-scale, technically demanding infrastructure opportunities

risks.risk: Heavy dependence on Government and PSU clients
risks.note: The disclosed client portfolio composition is skewed toward Government (36%) and PSU (58%) clients versus only 6% Private, i.e. ~94% combined public-sector exposure — a structural concentration that ties revenue realisation and order-award timing to government/PSU budget cycles, approvals and payment discipline rather than diversified private demand.

risks.risk: Recent change in ownership and control (integration risk)
risks.note: During FY 2025-26 the erstwhile Promoter, Italian-Thai Development Public Company Limited, divested its entire 46.64% stake to Renew Exim DMCC (Adani Group), which subsequently acquired a further 20.83% via open offer and took control effective May 28, 2025. This is a recent, large-scale change of promoter and control (accompanied by a company name/identity change), which carries integration and continuity risk even as management frames it as a strategic positive.

Management explicitly flags that it 'strives to remain vigilant on the evolving cyber security threat' to the Company's IT systems, within its internal financial controls disclosure — an acknowledged and evolving threat vector rather than a static, fully-mitigated risk.

one-line thesis: Cemindia crossed INR 10,000 Cr revenue with a 66% YoY EBITDA jump in Q4 driven by one-off claim realizations, while securing a record INR 19,000 Cr orders to expand the book to INR 29,000 Cr. Guidance points to 25% revenue growth in FY27, underpinned by a massive INR 70,000 Cr pipeline and new verticals like data centers, though sustainable margins are guided lower at 10.5% excluding one-offs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,973 Cr (Q4, +17% YoY), INR 10,061 Cr (FY26, +9% YoY); EBITDA: INR 450 Cr (Q4, +66% YoY), Margin 15.1% (vs 10.7% prior); PAT: INR 242 Cr (Q4, +114% YoY), INR 598 Cr (FY26, +60% YoY); Order Book: INR 29,000 Cr (up from ~21,000 Cr); Net Debt: Negligible (D/E 0.18%). One-offs: INR 100 Cr claim realization in Q4 (part of INR 150 Cr full year) inflated margins; provision reversals on completed metro projects contributed to 15.1% margin vs sustainable ~10.5%.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 25% for FY27; Margin: 10.5% sustainable EBITDA margin (excluding other income/one-offs); Order Inflow Target: INR 25,000 Cr for FY27; Capex: INR 350-400 Cr for FY27.
order book & pipeline: Total INR 29,000 Cr includes INR 1,600 Cr (L1 pending LoA) and INR 3,200 Cr (secured in April). Key wins: Delhi Metro Underground, Pune Metro, Kolkata Metro, JSW Port, Abu Dhabi overseas job, Bihar elevated road. Data Center segment contributes ~INR 3,000 Cr. Legacy low-margin jobs fully exited.
segment / subsidiary detail: Metro/Tunneling: Completed Bangalore, Mumbai, Udangudi; ongoing Chennai (4 TBMs deployed, 40% work left, completion 2028), Delhi, Pune. Marine: Vadhvan Port delayed (local issues), breakwater/dredging tenders pending. Data Centers: New division, 3-4 jobs secured from Adani Group (INR 3,000 Cr), focusing on group opportunities (e.g., Vizag). Roads: New Bihar elevated corridor (self-executed).
growth verticals / optionality: Pipeline of INR 70,000 Cr (35-40% from Adani Group). Major opportunities in large-diameter tunnels (market >INR 1 Lakh Cr), highways (market ~INR 1 Lakh Cr), and potential Navi Mumbai Airport Phase 2 bid. Data center civil works emerging as high-growth vertical within group ecosystem.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 margin (15.1%) boosted by INR 100 Cr claims and provision reversals; sustainable guidance reset to 10.5%. Cost escalation protection exists in ~80% of contracts (escalation clauses/star rates), but abnormal inflation (war/commodity spikes) remains a risk. Subcontracting minimal for key new road jobs.
capex / expansion: FY26 actual: INR 260 Cr. FY27 planned: INR 350-400 Cr. Primary use: Acquisition of new TBMs for Pune/Delhi Metro and potential large-diameter tunnel projects; current TBM fleet fully deployed (no idle capacity).
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.18%). No immediate fundraising plans. Dividend declaration delayed but expected within weeks. Focus on organic growth funding via internal accruals.
risks & watch-items: Vadhvan Port project delays (undefined timeline); Government payment cycles (state treasury issues vs. central reliability); Commodity inflation exceeding escalation clauses; Execution risk on record order book with limited idle TBM capacity; Dependency on Adani Group for ~40% of pipeline.
management quality / tone: Highly confident on order momentum and execution capabilities; transparent about one-off nature of Q4 margins; cautious on timing of tender conversions despite large pipeline; emphasized 'no legacy jobs' and clean balance sheet.
non-obvious takeaways: Data Center vertical already scaled to INR 3,000 Cr order book quietly within group; 90% of mobilization advances (INR 1,400 Cr total) are interest-free, improving working capital efficiency; TBM asset turnover is critical bottleneck with zero idle capacity.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraints in tunneling and marine EPC as order book hits record highs | NBCC (India) Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Potential subcontracting partner if Cemindia faces TBM bottlenecks, though Cemindia prefers self-execution. |
| Inflationary pressure on steel/cement impacting marginal EPC players without escalation clauses | Small-cap Civil Contractors | loser | Med | Cemindia's 80% clause coverage highlights vulnerability of smaller peers lacking pricing power. |
| Need for specialized data center construction as digital infra capex surges | Adani Enterprises Ltd | beneficiary | High | Parent company driving order flow to Cemindia for data centers; synergies benefit both entities. |

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.

growth_optionality.body: Pipeline of INR 70,000 Cr (35-40% from Adani Group). Major opportunities in large-diameter tunnels (market >INR 1 Lakh Cr), highways (market ~INR 1 Lakh Cr), and potential Navi Mumbai Airport Phase 2 bid. Data center civil works emerging as high-growth vertical within group ecosystem.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's infrastructure sector is entering a multi-decade investment cycle supported by transformative government initiatives such as the National Infrastructure Pipeline, Sagarmala, Bharatmala and PM Gati Shakti, driving opportunities across transportation, urban infrastructure, maritime structures and data centres
- FY 2025-26 performance marks a strategic transition toward high-value mega-projects, which management says is driving considerable margin expansion and superior execution quality
- Structural challenges flagged by management include macroeconomic volatility, input cost fluctuations, working capital intensity and industry-wide skill shortages, mitigated through disciplined bidding, prudent financial management and sustained investment in talent and operational capabilities
- Integration into the Adani Group is expected to enhance the ability to undertake larger, more complex, multidisciplinary infrastructure projects while preserving engineering discipline and execution excellence
- Total value of new contracts secured during FY 2025-26 exceeded Rs 14,821 crores, including several major contracts of Rs 200 crores and above across metro tunnels (West Bengal, Pune), water intake systems (Uttar Pradesh), a four-laning road project (Bihar), port/berth and breakwater works (Odisha, Kerala), data centres (Maharashtra), and international jetty and container terminal works (Abu Dhabi, Colombo)
- During the year a number of contracts were completed, including underground metro sections in Mumbai and Kolkata, a rubble mound breakwater in Kerala, a bulk berth at Dhamra (Odisha), a marine jetty in Tamil Nadu, container terminal works in Colombo (Sri Lanka), and the Brahmaputra riverfront development in Assam
- The Company is systematically diversifying its project portfolio across geographies and high-growth sectors to capture large-scale, technically demanding infrastructure opportunities

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 margin (15.1%) boosted by INR 100 Cr claims and provision reversals; sustainable guidance reset to 10.5%. Cost escalation protection exists in ~80% of contracts (escalation clauses/star rates), but abnormal inflation (war/commodity spikes) remains a risk. Subcontracting minimal for key new road jobs.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.18%). No immediate fundraising plans. Dividend declaration delayed but expected within weeks. Focus on organic growth funding via internal accruals.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26, Cemindia secured record order inflows of Rs 14,821 crores, taking the order book to an all-time high of Rs 24,545 crores as of March 31, 2026, spanning a diversified project mix across maritime structures, metro rail, airports, highways/bridges/flyovers, industrial structures and buildings, hydro dams/tunnels/irrigation, water and wastewater, foundation and specialist engineering, and data centres. Major new orders secured during the year include a four-laning road project in Bihar, the Pune underground metro (Maharashtra), EPC of a data centre in Maharashtra, the Kolkata underground metro (West Bengal), bulk and breakwater works for a Greenfield captive jetty in Odisha, airport works at Jaipur International Airport (Rajasthan) and Trivandrum International Airport (Kerala), LNG jetty works in Abu Dhabi, breakwater and container berth Phase II works at Vizhinjam (Kerala), and a multi-storeyed commercial building in Kolkata. The Company is expanding into the fast-growing data centre segment, including 80 MW (NMI-03) and 30 MW (NMI-01) data centres at Ghansoli, Maharashtra. Growth is supported by continued investment in a modern, specialised construction equipment fleet (Tunnel Boring Machines, trench cutters, jack-up barges, batching plants, hydraulic piling rigs) and digital execution tools (Building Information Modelling, IoT-enabled asset intelligence, UAV site monitoring, and an integrated Project Management Information System). Capital expenditure directed toward technologies that improve environmental and social impact rose to 6.33% of total capex in FY26 from 3.90% in FY25 (BRSR Principle 2), including adoption of BSVI-compliant diesel generator sets and an HVS Rotating Laser Machine (150 metre) to improve construction quality and efficiency.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident on order momentum and execution capabilities; transparent about one-off nature of Q4 margins; cautious on timing of tender conversions despite large pipeline; emphasized 'no legacy jobs' and clean balance sheet.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over 90-year civil engineering legacy and execution track record across maritime structures, metro rail, airports, highways, bridges/flyovers, industrial structures, data centres, hydro dams, tunnels and irrigation
- Strategic integration with the Adani Group providing enhanced financial strength, improved access to capital, shared procurement capabilities, global vendor networks and early visibility into a large infrastructure project pipeline
- Diversified, all-time high order book of Rs 24,545 crores across a geographically spread footprint (16 Indian states plus Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and UAE)
- Technology-enabled execution framework: Building Information Modelling (BIM), IoT-enabled asset intelligence, UAV site monitoring, and an integrated Project Management Information System (PMIS)
- Modern, specialised construction equipment fleet including Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs), trench cutters, jack-up barges, batching plants and hydraulic piling rigs
- Large, experienced professional workforce of 3,187 permanent employees plus 33,621 contractual personnel
- Well-balanced client mix across government (58%), PSU (36%) and private (6%) clients mitigating concentration risk

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Vadhvan Port project delays (undefined timeline); Government payment cycles (state treasury issues vs. central reliability); Commodity inflation exceeding escalation clauses; Execution risk on record order book with limited idle TBM capacity; Dependency on Adani Group for ~40% of pipeline.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Data Center vertical already scaled to INR 3,000 Cr order book quietly within group; 90% of mobilization advances (INR 1,400 Cr total) are interest-free, improving working capital efficiency; TBM asset turnover is critical bottleneck with zero idle capacity.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraints in tunneling and marine EPC as order book hits record highs | NBCC (India) Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Potential subcontracting partner if Cemindia faces TBM bottlenecks, though Cemindia prefers self-execution. |
| Inflationary pressure on steel/cement impacting marginal EPC players without escalation clauses | Small-cap Civil Contractors | loser | Med | Cemindia's 80% clause coverage highlights vulnerability of smaller peers lacking pricing power. |
| Need for specialized data center construction as digital infra capex surges | Adani Enterprises Ltd | beneficiary | High | Parent company driving order flow to Cemindia for data centers; synergies benefit both entities. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Rebrand] The company has been renamed Cemindia Projects Limited, formerly ITD Cementation India Limited, and now trades under the NSE symbol CEMPRO / BSE code 509496.
- [Ownership] A change of ownership into the Adani ecosystem is cited by the rating agencies as a driver of growth synergies and stronger financial flexibility.
- [Board] Leadership is Adani-linked and newly configured — Malay Mahadevia as Chairman, Jayanta Basu as Managing Director (39+ years), with independent directors Manoj Kumar Kohli, Sangeeta Bhatia and Abizer Diwanji.
- [Governance] Three additional non-statutory committees have been created — IT & Data Security, Corporate Responsibility, and Legal, Regulatory & Tax.
